stem: A very early node-associated structure is visible but does not yet show enough detail for confident reproductive classification. What should the observer do?
choices: Map and document the structure, mark the classification as uncertain, and repeat the observation as it develops
Classify it from the cultivar name
Assume it is pistillate because the seed was sold as feminized
Remove the structure immediately to avoid uncertainty
rationale: Direct morphology should drive reproductive classification. Early structures can be ambiguous, so repeat observation preserves accuracy and avoids unsupported certainty.
